target_customer: Middle market general contractors and builders (about $25M to $250M of projects per year) buying excess and primary casualty, builder's risk and pollution coverage
problem: Construction insurance is slow, opaque and priced off legacy books. Shepherd underwrites with project and technology data and started with excess liability, where the CEO said the pain was greatest.
business_model: Managing general underwriter and insurer earning premium and fees on commercial construction policies

founders.name: Justin Levine
founders.background_notes: Carrier Management (Nov 2021) links him to building technology for subcontractor prequalification for construction risk managers.

founders.name: Mo Mahallawy
founders.background_notes: The YC page gives no background. Carrier Management says one of three co-founders was a former Airbnb software engineer but does not say which.

founders.name: Stephen Buonpane
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder by Carrier Management. The article describes one co-founder as a former construction insurance underwriter without naming which.

technical_complexity.rationale: Underwriting software and broker platform on top of partner carrier paper is standard engineering, with the hard parts being pricing models and regulatory structure as a managing general underwriter.

defensibility.rationale: Carrier capacity, underwriting data accumulated over policies and broker relationships are slow to copy, but at founding there was no book of business, which the CEO presented as a pricing advantage over legacy insurers.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: TechCrunch (Sept 2021) refers to incumbents with legacy books raising prices rather than copying the model. Intact, a carrier, later became an investor and casualty partner.

market_need_then: TechCrunch (Sept 2021) describes incumbents with legacy books raising prices and a hard market for excess liability for contractors. Procore, a construction software firm, invested and partnered.

branding.domain_note: Company used withshepherd.com in early years and shepherdinsurance.com later; an unrelated Shepherd Insurance agency founded 1977 exists. No acquisition history found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and builder focused: 'Making risk frictionless'

branding.brand_signature: Shepherd Savings program rewarding builders that invest in technology

brand_strength.rationale: Insurance buyers choose through brokers and the brand is a generic word shared with other insurers, but press coverage and investor backing built credibility. No source shows the brand itself driving growth.

outcome_analysis: Shepherd entered a hard market where incumbents were raising prices, started with excess liability, and used a seed in 2021 backed by a construction software partner. It added product lines, grew written premium, and raised a Series A in 2024 and a $42M Series B in 2026 with a carrier as lead. The company states about $67M raised in total, and the trajectory is strongly positive but not yet an exit.
notes: Series A amount and lead come from several outlets surfaced in search (SiliconANGLE, Pulse 2, Insurtech Digital, FinTech Futures press release); the press release page returned 403 and was not opened. Company stated total raised is $67M as of the Series B; aggregators list lower totals. Competitor lists on aggregators (Getsurance, Advisr and others) are undated and unverified, and neither the TechCrunch seed article nor Carrier Management names rivals, so the dated list is empty. The company's address in the YC page is San Francisco. Stephen Buonpane appears as a co-founder in Carrier Management and company investor posts but not on the YC page.
